## Goals

- Visualize relationships between two or more variables
- Use faceting to compare patterns across groups
- Choose plot types deliberately, not by habit

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
data(iris)
iris <- as_tibble(iris)
```
:::



## Two numeric variables: relationships



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Sepal length vs. petal length](week04-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-scatter-1.png){#fig-scatter width=672}
:::
:::



## Many variables: faceting



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~Species) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Sepal length vs. width, faceted by species](week04-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-facet-1.png){#fig-facet width=672}
:::
:::



## Choosing a plot deliberately

A quick decision guide, roughly in order of how often you'll reach
for it in this course:

| You have... | Reach for... |
|---|---|
| One numeric variable | Histogram or density plot |
| One numeric + one categorical | Boxplot or jittered points |
| Two numeric variables | Scatterplot (+ trend line) |
| A relationship that differs by group | Scatterplot colored by group, or `facet_wrap()` |
| A variable over time, per individual | Line plot grouped by individual ID |

## Exercises

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 1
Using `ChickWeight`, plot `weight` vs. `Time` with one line per chick
(`geom_line()`, grouped by `Chick`), colored by `Diet`. What pattern
do you see?
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 2
Pick one plot from this week or last week's tutorial and rewrite it
with better axis labels, a descriptive title, and a
colorblind-friendly palette (`scale_color_viridis_d()` /
`scale_fill_viridis_d()`).
:::
